title: VMF wave schedule
description: SCHED-1, SCHEDULE-START-ONCE-1, SCHEDULE-SCHEMA-1. When a wave starts, at schedules/<wave>.json in the run. Set-VmfWaveSchedule writes it as 'pending' (the service, when a person schedules the wave). The service's schedule pass writes the start into it before it starts the wave ('starting', with a new start id that the start carries to Azure), then the executions after it ('started'), each write version-checked (Set-VmfScheduleStartRecord). The start carries the version of the wave the pass judged (VMF_WAVE_VERSION): the engine run of that start removes the schedule when its own read of the wave is that version (Remove-VmfScheduleOfStart), and sets it to 'pending' again, with no start on record, when it is not, so the wave stays scheduled (Reset-VmfScheduleStartRecord -StartId, SCHEDULE-WAVE-VERSION-1). The service removes a schedule with a start on record only when no engine run of that start goes on. A start that was not made and that a check then stops (the window, the approval, a change after the sign-off) goes back to 'pending' with no start on record (Reset-VmfScheduleStartRecord, SCHEDULE-STARTING-STUCK-1). A cancel removes a pending schedule; a cancel or a new time is refused while a start is on record. Read by the service (Get-VmfScheduleStep, Invoke-VmfFacadeReleaseDueSchedules), the plan continue rule (Get-VmfPlanRunDecision, through Get-VmfWaveSchedule), the wave editor save (Set-VmfWavePlan removes a schedule of a wave that no longer exists) and the migration page. Every time is UTC, written as the round-trip ('o') text. MIGRATION NOTE: the document had schemaVersion 1 before this schema; the schema describes it as it is, and nothing is rewritten.

wave.description: The wave the schedule starts. The file name is the same wave.

runAtUtc.description: When the wave is to start. In the future when it is written; the pass starts the wave on its first pass at or after this time.

scheduledBy.description: The user who scheduled the wave, as the service gives it; 'unknown' when it gives none. The scheduled start runs as 'schedule (<this>)'.

note.description: Why the wave is scheduled. A schedule requires a note.

windowMinutes.description: The time window in minutes. A wave the engine estimates cannot finish inside it does not start, and stays scheduled. Null when the schedule has no window.

state.description: pending: the wave waits for its time. starting: the pass wrote the start, and starts or started the engine; a start that was not made and that a check then stops goes back to pending. started: the pass started the engine. The engine run of the start removes the schedule, or sets it to pending again when its read of the wave differs from the version the pass judged; the service removes it after that run.

startId.description: The id of the start, a new one each time the pass writes 'starting'. The engine start carries it to Azure (VMF_SCHEDULE_START), so a later pass can ask Azure whether the start was made.

startingUtc.description: When the pass wrote 'starting'. A starting record younger than the grace period (10 minutes) with no execution in Azure is left alone.

executions.description: The engine executions that the start made. Empty while the state is 'starting'.

startedUtc.description: When the pass wrote 'started'. Null while the state is 'starting'.

then.description: A pending schedule has no start on record: Set-VmfWaveSchedule writes the whole document, and refuses to write over a start.
